title: Google fined €403m by Irish data watchdog over location tracking
description: Google has been fined €403m (£345m) by the Republic of Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) over its handling of location data.The penalty - one
body: Google has been fined €403m (£345m) by the Republic of Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) over its handling of location data.The penalty - one of the largest of its kind imposed by the Irish watchdog authority -  followed an inquiry launched into the tech giant six years ago, following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations.On Monday the DPC said its investigation found Google had processed data in a manner that was not "lawful", "fair" or "transparent".The inquiry concerned Google's processing of location data in three specific features - Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy between 25 May 2018 to 4 February 2020.Location data is any kind of data which can be used to infer a person's location. It can "reveal a significant amount of information about an individual, including information that is inherently private", said DPC deputy commissioner Graham Doyle in a statement released on Monday.The report said Google's practices "infringed" General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - legislation that came into effect on 25 May, 2018, creating strict data privacy and security law within the European Union (EU).Doyle added: "The GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) provides a high level of protection of personal data throughout the EEA (European Economic Area), and requires that the processing of personal data must be carried out in a lawful, fair and transparent manner."He continued: "As a result of Google's failures... individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data."The retention of users' location data for longer than necessary aggravated this loss of control."In addition to being fined, Google has also been ordered to bring its data processing into compliance within six months.

schema.headline: Google fined €403m by Irish data watchdog over location tracking

title: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon: Trial of policeman accused of double murder begins in Sydney
description: A former police officer accused of using his work gun to kill a Sydney couple was driven by a "jealous infatuation" with his ex, a court has heard.Bea
body: A former police officer accused of using his work gun to kill a Sydney couple was driven by a "jealous infatuation" with his ex, a court has heard.Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to two charges of domestic violence-related murder and one of aggravated break and enter. Prosecutors allege Lamarre-Condon shot his ex-partner, 26-year-old TV presenter Jesse Baird, and Baird's new partner Luke Davies, a 29-year-old Qantas flight attendant, at a home in the Sydney suburb of Paddington in 2024.The couple's bodies were found in a rural area 200km away, hidden in surfboard bags. The trial is expected to run for three months.In his opening address on Monday, prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC described how Lamarre-Condon had developed an "obsessive and jealous infatuation" with Baird after a brief romantic relationship.It manifested itself in a "range of compulsive behaviour", Hatfield said, which escalated when Baird ended all contact in November 2023.The barrister said Lamarre-Condon used a friend's phone to message Baird and claim he had cancer, stalked his ex-lover, and tampered with his car in the weeks after their break-up.On the day of the alleged murders, Lamarre-Condon had set his alarm for 04.30 local time, Hatfield claimed, and sent a text to a friend which read: "I'll try to call you tonight and update you... there's no sign I'm doing it".Lamarre-Condon then switched to a burner phone, picked up a rental car and waited outside Baird's home for three hours dressed as an Uber driver, the prosecution alleged. He had previously bought a surfboard bag to dispose of Baird's body, Hatfield said.After entering Baird's home with a key he had previously obtained, Lamarre-Condon shot Baird in the kitchen and then killed Davies in the bedroom as he was trying to call emergency services for help, the court was told. Hatfield said that the accused had planned Baird's murder, and killed Davies so as to "eliminate him as a witness".In the hours and days after the alleged killings, Lamarre-Condon tried to cover up the murder, Hatfield said, including sending messages from Baird's mobile phone.The aggravated break and enter charge that Lamarre-Condon is facing refers to an incident in August 2023 where it's alleged he broke into Baird's home and stole his phone and wallet.Hatfield also told the court that Lamarre-Condon had earlier offered to plead guilty to a single charge of manslaughter relating to Baird's death but this was rejected.Police were first alerted to the alleged murders after bloodied items belonging to Baird and Davies were found in a bin in Sydney's south.Later that week, Lamarre-Condon handed himself in to a police station and was charged. Eight days after the alleged killings took place, authorities found the couple's bodies.Lamarre-Condon was sacked by New South Wales Police in the weeks after he was charged with the alleged murders.Before the opening address on Monday, a 15-member jury was selected, with the judge, Justice Natalie Adams, explaining that three extra people were chosen - a jury is typically made up of 12 people - as a contingency for sickness and other unforeseen circumstances.

schema.headline: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon: Trial of policeman accused of double murder begins in Sydney

title: Death of Cindy Crawford's son Presley Gerber being investigated as suspected overdose
description: Figure caption, Watch: Presley Gerber seen alongside his family on the red carpetByChris Graham and Grace Eliza GoodwinUpdated 3 hours agoOfficials ar
body: Figure caption, Watch: Presley Gerber seen alongside his family on the red carpetByChris Graham and Grace Eliza GoodwinUpdated 3 hours agoOfficials are investigating the death of Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, as a suspected overdose, Santa Monica police said on Monday. The 27-year-old model died at a rehab facility on Sunday, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. The exact cause of death has not been determined, police said, adding there was no indication of foul play.Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and her husband Rande Gerber, told the BBC's US partner CBS News: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Presley Gerber became a model like his mother and sisterHe went on to model for brands including Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana, and Bottega Veneta.His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.In recent years, Presley Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use. In 2023, he told the Studio 22 podcast: "Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do." And in this month's American Vogue, external, Kaia discussed her brother's struggles with addiction. She said: "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone."I think that's also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help."She added: "My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn't share anything - and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, 'I'm gonna be very human for everyone.' There's only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you're ashamed of them."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Gerber (left) was a model and had spoken about his close relationship with his familyGerber had previously spoken of his close relationship with his family, including Kaia, who he appeared alongside in a campaign for Calvin Klein in 2018, and whose name he had tattooed on his arm.He told People Magazine that year: "We're a close family, especially me and my sister, so it's definitely cool. "We get to travel together half of the time, so it makes it a lot less lonely."Gerber also starred alongside his mother in Pepsi's 2018 Super Bowl commercial, 26 years after Crawford first appeared in her famous 1992 advertisement for the brand."We're a really tight family, so it was just like going to work with one of your friends. It was so fun, and easy," he told People Magazine at the time.In July, Crawford shared two childhood photographs of her son on Instagram to mark his 27th birthday."I'm so proud of the man you've become, but I'll always see you as my little boy! Love you," she wrote.If you are suffering distress or despair, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

schema.headline: Death of Cindy Crawford's son Presley Gerber being investigated as suspected overdose

title: Aleema Khanum: Sister of Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan arrested
description: The sister of Pakistan's imprisoned former prime minister, Imran Khan, has been arrested ahead of next week's protests held in his support, his Pakist
body: The sister of Pakistan's imprisoned former prime minister, Imran Khan, has been arrested ahead of next week's protests held in his support, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party has said.Aleema Khanum was detained in the eastern city of Lahore on Sunday afternoon, PTI officials said, calling it an "illegal detention". Her son is demanding her return.The order for Khanum's arrest, which came from Lahore's deputy commissioner, alleged that she was mobilising Imran Khan's supporters "through social media and public meetings". It added that she will be detained for 30 days.Khanum is a vocal critic of her brother's detention, regularly speaking to his supporters and the media. A police official confirmed Khanum's arrest to the BBC. According to the order, she will be taken to Kot Lakhpat jail in Lahore. Earlier in the day, her family said they had had "no contact or news of her whereabouts". "We demand the government immediately disclose her whereabouts and ensure her safe return," Khanum's son Shahrez Khan wrote on X.Many have linked her arrest to the protests that have been organised across the country on 27 September, when demonstrators plan to march to the Pakistani capital, Islamabad.The arrest order said Khanum had been mobilising people to "create law and order situations" and "raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the Government."Streets in Islamabad are already lined with shipping containers, ready to safeguard the city's government buildings. Local media has reported Pakistan's interior minister as saying that the protests harm the country and that the government will do everything they can to stop them.Khan has been detained since 2023, when he was sentenced to three years in prison for not declaring money earned from selling gifts he had received while in office. He has faced charges in over 100 cases, ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts - all of which he has decried as politically motivated.Last year, the cricket star-turned-politician was jailed for 14 years in a land corruption case - the longest sentence he has received.While in prison, his health has being deteriorating, and last month Khan had to visit a hospital for an examination.

schema.headline: Aleema Khanum: Sister of Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan arrested

title: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex
description: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipersFigure caption, A look at the design plans for Trump's triumphal arch as pro
body: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipersFigure caption, A look at the design plans for Trump's triumphal arch as proposed in AprilByGrace Eliza GoodwinUS President Donald Trump has said his proposed triumphal arch will double as a complex to store military equipment, complete with the ability to deploy snipers and drones.In a Sunday morning post, Trump said he is updating the plans at the "strong request" of the US military and for "national security purposes".The "top grade" military complex and arch will "house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage", he said.He did not provide details on construction plans or timing, and it's not clear if he needs further approval for the facility.Image source, Getty Images"There will be no facility like this anywhere in the World," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. He added that out of "the 59 top cities and Capitals", Washington DC is "the only one in the world that does not have a triumphal arch", without specifying what those cities are. Construction on Trump's 250-foot arch, planned for a site across the Potomac River from Washington DC just outside the Arlington National Cemetery, was expected to begin this month. A rendering of the design from earlier this year includes a golden, winged Lady Liberty on the top of the arch, flanked by two gold eagles, and with the phrases "One Nation Under God" and "Liberty and Justice for All" inscribed in gold on either side of the structure. It will stand 250-feet (76m) from its base to the top of the golden lady statue.At that height, the structure would dwarf the 99-foot Lincoln Memorial nearby and be half as high as the Washington Monument.Image caption, Plans for the arch from earlier this year feature a golden, winged Lady Liberty on the top, flanked by two gold eagles.The Department of Defence declined to provide additional details when reached for comment.Trump has pursued a number of construction projects during his second term to revamp the US capital, including a gilded makeover of the Oval Office, constructing a White House ballroom estimated to cost around $400m, paving over the White House Rose Garden, and renovating the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.The triumphal arch is one of the biggest projects Trump has set his sights on.

schema.headline: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex

title: Ekurhuleni killings: Two charged with murder in South Africa over woman's body in Dawn Park
description: Two women have been charged in South Africa in connection with the murder of a woman in an area east of Johannesburg – the last of nine recent cases i
body: Two women have been charged in South Africa in connection with the murder of a woman in an area east of Johannesburg – the last of nine recent cases in that region that have reignited the debate about the levels of gender-based violence in the country.Under pressure to solve the spate of murders which has involved victims' bodies being dumped on a roadside, police have described the arrests of the two as a "breakthrough".Referring to all nine cases, acting police chief Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane said her officers were "working tirelessly to bring those responsible to justice".The two women have been charged with premeditated murder and defeating the ends of justice.A man who was also arrested has been released without charge.Their case relates to the death of Jabulile Ntimba, whose half-naked body was found wrapped in a sheet in Dawn Park last Thursday.Several of the recent victims were discovered partially clothed and with injuries, but police have stressed that they have not established whether all the deaths are connected or whether a serial killer is responsible.Addressing journalists on Monday, deputy police chief Lt Gen Tebello Mosikili said that "a team of analysts are working hard to see if there are links to all these cases" but the killing of Ntimba "appears to be an indication of a murder that stemmed from a relationship... this includes... a possible love triangle".South Africa has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world. It also has a very high murder rate and though officials statistics do not identify the gender of the victims, a recent estimate from the country's Human Rights Commission indicated that, on average, six women were murdered every day between April and June this year.The recent grim discoveries have sparked a national outcry about the scale of the problem and increased the feeling of insecurity for many women.

schema.headline: Ekurhuleni killings: Two charged with murder in South Africa over woman's body in Dawn Park

title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
description: Ukraine has fired its largest drone attack on the Moscow region, the mayor has said, hitting the city's main oil refinery and a residential building.M
body: Ukraine has fired its largest drone attack on the Moscow region, the mayor has said, hitting the city's main oil refinery and a residential building.Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 450 drones heading for the capital had been shot down in what he called "the most massive" attack. The region's governor said at least two people were killed and 20 injured.Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Kyiv had hit a "key" Russian oil facility and a logistics site in the region with drones and missiles, representing "billions of dollars that sustain the war machine".Ukrainian officials meanwhile said nine people, including three children, had been killed in Russian attacks in the Kyiv and Sumy regions on Saturday.Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.A 44-year-old woman was killed in Sofyino on Sunday after a drone hit a three-storey residential building, regional head Andrei Vorobyev said. Another five people - including two children - were injured.An elderly man died after a private house was hit in the Orekhovo-Zuevo district, Governor Andrei Vorobyev added.Videos verified by the BBC on social media show explosions in the night skies above Moscow, and a burning warehouse.Mayor Sobyanin said a drone had struck a building near one of the capital's boulevards and the oil refinery - where Ukrainian military officials said three key units had been damaged.The site supplies more than a third of the Moscow region's fuel, according to the defence ministry in Kyiv, and some of its petrol, diesel and aviation fuel go to Russia's military.Ukraine's defence minister said attacking such facilities "directly undermines the enemy's ability to continue its war of aggression and supply its military formations".Sobyanin said the major attack was "an attempt to disrupt" Russia's parliamentary election, which was in its third day on Sunday. The vote is tightly controlled by the Kremlin and has been dismissed by critics as neither free, fair nor transparent.Russian state media reported that an election official was one of two people killed by a drone attack on a bus in a Moscow-controlled part of Kherson in Ukraine on Sunday, citing the head of Russia's election commission.Meanwhile, Moscow's biggest airport Sheremetyevo warned passengers "temporary restrictions" were in place overnight, while at the capital's Vnukovo airport all arrivals and departures were halted. Restrictions at both airports were lifted by Sunday morning but each warned some flights may still be delayed.It comes after a mother and her two small children, a boy and a girl, were killed in a Russian attack in the city of Fastiv, Kyiv on Saturday, according to regional head Tymur Tkachenko.He later said a child injured in a separate attack in Vyshhorod, north of Kyiv, had also died in hospital.In the north-eastern Sumy region, four people were killed when a Russian drone hit the car they were travelling in, top local official Oleh Hryhorov said.Russia also struck a monastery in the Kherson region with a drone on Saturday, Zelensky said, killing one member of the clergy and injuring four others.Both Russia and Ukraine have continued to hit energy infrastructure targets in the past week, despite US President Donald Trump claiming on social media that the two sides had agreed not to do so.Trump signed a sanctions bill on Friday that targets Russia's economy by implementing tariffs on the biggest buyers of the country's oil and gas which include China and India.The US legislation gives the US president powers to impose 100% tariffs on major purchasers of Russian energy.Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

schema.headline: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says

title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of first Trump meeting in US
description: "Donald Trump is trying to claim he's got a success in Greenland, but actually, all he's got is almost a carbon copy of the agreement that's persisted
body: "Donald Trump is trying to claim he's got a success in Greenland, but actually, all he's got is almost a carbon copy of the agreement that's persisted since the 1950s," he said during a Q&A at the Lib Dem party conference."So let Donald Trump try to pretend he's had a victory. The truth is, Europe, Nato, countries like Canada stood up to him and won."Trump had for months threatened to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.Following the announcement of the deal, Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.Burnham has spoken to Trump at least twice since entering Downing Street and No 10 said he intended to use the UNGA to "drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home", including the cost of living and the war in Ukraine.

schema.headline: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of first Trump meeting in US

title: Merz vows to keep ruling coalition together for sake of Germany's 'democratic future'
description: Speaking at the news conference on Monday, Merz described the result in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern as "a heavy blow" for the centre-right CDU. "This elect
body: Speaking at the news conference on Monday, Merz described the result in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern as "a heavy blow" for the centre-right CDU. "This election is a profound turning point. It is a dramatic, unprecedented result for the CDU in Germany," he acknowledged.Merz said there had been no discussion about his own position since the results and pushed back against the idea that his low popularity ratings alone were behind the election defeats."I know that I as an individual played a role in these state elections," Merz said, before adding: "But the reasons for the results go far beyond just me.""We are witnessing a profound transformation of Germany's political party system, as is happening in many other countries around the world."There have been rumours Merz, who has only been in power for 16 months, could be replaced mid-term in a so-called chancellor swap due to his poor approval ratings.Asked earlier on Monday how long Merz has left in office, the AfD's co-leader Alice Weidel told the BBC: "Pretty soon, he's going to leave."The two elections took place on Sunday, a fortnight after the CDU saw its vote halved in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD won a major victory.In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the CDU fell short of a 5% threshold to enter parliament, underperforming against what had already been projected to be the party's worst ever result in the area. Merz earlier conceded that this result was "a disaster".While the AfD won the most votes in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, it was far short of a majority and is unlikely to govern as other parties may refuse to work with it.Some branches of the party are classed as right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence, a designation it strongly rejects. But its anti-immigration, Germany first, and Russian-friendly agenda has found fertile ground in the country's former communist east.In Berlin, the CDU's defeat means Die Linke, which won the most votes, could now take power in a coalition. Elif Eralp, who led the party to victory in the capital, promised to tackle unaffordable rent prices in remarks made after the results came out."The people of Berlin have clearly opted for a change in policy, specifically for an affordable Berlin, for policies that solve the rent crisis and put people first," she told German news outlet The Pioneer.During the election campaign, Eralp pledged to expropriate more than 200,000 housing units from private landlords. Merz has promised to pursue legislation to prevent such actions, citing the impact on foreign investment.

schema.headline: Merz vows to keep ruling coalition together for sake of Germany's 'democratic future'

title: Millions urged to evacuate as Typhoon Dujuan hits Japan
description: Figure caption, Watch: Timelapse shows typhoon barrelling towards JapanByJamie Whitehead  and Kurumi MoriTokyo correspondent Updated 2 hours agoAlmost
body: Figure caption, Watch: Timelapse shows typhoon barrelling towards JapanByJamie Whitehead  and Kurumi MoriTokyo correspondent Updated 2 hours agoAlmost two million people are under evacuation orders in Japan as Typhoon Dujuan batters a number of the country's prefectures.The country's public broadcaster, NHK, reported that two people had died and four others were missing as a result of the typhoon. It also reported four were missing in Kanagawa prefecture.  Japan's Meteorological Agency had warned of an "imminent threat to life", but several weather warnings have now been downgraded.Strong winds caused power cuts for more than 50,000 people, while hundreds of flights have been cancelled and rail services have been suspended. Dujuan has had sustained winds of 130km/h (80.8mph) and gusts of 194 km/h.Image source, EPAImage caption, Pedestrians caught in the rain at the Shibuya crossing in Tokyo The typhoon is the latest in a series of storms in the Pacific, made more intense by the "super El Niño", which has warmed the ocean, fuelling the formation of storms.Authorities have advised the public to pay attention to weather information. Dujuan, which is Japan's 25th typhoon of the year, has hit in the midst of a five-day holiday and forced the cancellation of several events.Concerts scheduled for Monday at the Rock in Japan music festival have been cancelled, while the Tokyo Game Show, a video game convention, has also cancelled Monday's programme.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered her condolences in a post on X to those who lost thier lives in the typhoon, before saying she would be continuing with her scheduled trip the United States as planned.  "With a sense of urgency, I instructed Chief Cabinet Secretary Takehara and Minister Hosono to respond with utmost preparedness," she wrote, before saying she had boarded a flight to the US. She will be speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, and will meet with US President Donald Trump.  Image source, ReutersImage caption, Passengers waiting for updates at Haneda AirportThe Yokosuka City Fire Department told the BBC that a woman who lived in the house, aged in her 60s, may have been swept away and is believed to have been buried alive. Following a search by rescue crews, she was found inside the home and pronounced dead, NHK reported. Separately, Sodegaura City Fire Department in Chiba prefecture told the BBC a man in his 50s was rescued after getting trapped while working to clear debris at a landslide site.The department said the worker fell into a bamboo thicket, along with some heavy machinery. He was then taken to hospital before his death was confirmed, according to local reports. Police are investigating the details of the incident.Firefighters in Kanagawa prefecture said they received a call from a man who reported his house had been crushed by a landslide. Image source, EPAImage caption, A woman struggles with her umbrella outside Shinjuku stationSome research suggests that Japan has become more exposed to destructive storms, but climate change is not thought to be increasing the number of these storms globally, and could even make them less common in some regions.As temperatures rise, typhoons that do form are likely to become more intense on average, however.Warmer ocean waters mean storms can pick up more energy, leading to higher wind speeds.And because a warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, these storms could also bring heavier rainfall.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Another woman also struggles with an umbrella in Chiba This year, El Niño - the natural weather phenomenon bringing warmer water to parts of the tropical Pacific - is another factor.El Niño doesn't have a clear effect on the total number of typhoons, but it can affect where typhoons form, their strength and which countries they hit.Some El Niño events may expose Japan to stronger typhoons, for example.The typhoon is continuing to travel along the country's Pacific coast, heading north. The extent of the damage today may not be known until Tuesday. Additional reporting by Chie Kobayashi and Mark Poynting, climate reporter

schema.headline: Millions urged to evacuate as Typhoon Dujuan hits Japan

title: Friedrich Merz's political crisis threatens Germany's obsession with stability
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The German chancellor's political future hangs in the balance after bruising election defeatsByKatya AdlerEur
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The German chancellor's political future hangs in the balance after bruising election defeatsByKatya AdlerEurope editorGermany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz is a political record-breaker.The problem for him is these records are overwhelmingly negative and he is at risk of losing his job over them.The problem for the EU and for Europe more broadly is this has a destabilising effect far further afield.At a paltry 13%, Merz's popularity rating is the lowest for any German chancellor since polling began. German voters' ardour for him started lower and fell faster than any of his predecessors. The former corporate lawyer is perceived by many to be arrogant and out of touch with their problems.He has only been in government for 16 months but under his chairmanship, Merz's conservative Christian Democratic Unionist (CDU) party has suffered three very poor showings in regional elections over the last couple of weeks. The state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern broke another record on Sunday according to preliminary results: Merz's conservative CDU party did not even reach the 5% threshold to enter the regional parliament.Conversely, the anti-immigration, nationalist right Alternative for Germany (AfD) - a political party Merz had promised to slash support for when he was running for CDU leadership - has performed spectacularly well. It became the biggest political faction in two out of those three recent state elections and broke another record: they have a chance at governing in one of those states, Saxony Anhalt, despite the German authorities labelling them in part anti-democratic and far-right extremist.The AfD also tops opinion polls nationally, a particularly sensitive issue for Germany after its Nazi past.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The AfD, led by Tino Chrupalla and Alice Weidel, has surged in national opinion pollsThe party rejects the far-right label. Its German name, Alternative fuer Deutschland, means Alternative for Germany. That is exactly what they say voters now want.Following this month's regional election surge in success for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, plus its gains in Berlin - where the victors were the hard left Die Linke party - AfD co-leader Alice Weidel said on Monday that her party had effectively replaced the center-right CDU as Germany's true Volkspartei, or catch-all people's party.The AfD accuses Merz of  failing to fulfil his key election promises to improve the spluttering German economy - once seen as the financial engine of Europe - and to find workable solutions to voter fears about immigration and security on their streets.High time for political change, says the AfD.Merz's position as German chancellor certainly looks wobbly. There have been rumours for weeks of a brewing palace coup, where he would be replaced by a more popular CDU politician. Possible candidate names are swirling but no individual will stick out his or her neck in public until they know they have the backing of the party.I have reported on Germany for decades. This is a stability-obsessed country. This kind of political upheaval is deeply unusual. Even if Merz stays in post, his political clout and credibility, his room for manoeuvre inside a fractious coalition government, will be restricted.Looking uncharacteristically forlorn on Sunday evening, Merz jumped to make a televised address even before the regional election results were confirmed.He would press ahead with tax, welfare and economic reforms to bring about prosperity, he said. "Backbone, steadfastness and patience" were required.Figure caption, Why Merz is staying on as German chancellor after election 'disaster'But German patience is running thin.Voters in Germany, as across much of Europe, have repeatedly elected traditional parties of the centre-left, such as Germany's SPD party, or centre-right, like the CDU, since World War Two - but increasingly they feel let-down and frustrated as they fear for their economic future.Voter resentment really started to mount after the financial crisis of 2007/8, when these traditional parties were seen bailing out big banks, while families felt their savings and living standards dropped. Then came the 2015 migration crisis, when more than one million refugees and other migrants arrived by people-smuggler boats across the Mediterranean and made their way across Europe, often by foot, trying to settle in wealthier countries like Germany and Sweden. Germany took in one million people.Integration into German society has been mixed and Germans have been shocked and scared by a number of headline-making attacks by migrants over the years, some with a history of mental illness, others linked by the German authorities to Islamist extremist groups or ideology. In December, for example, police said they arrested five individuals suspected of plotting a Christmas market attack in Munich "based on an Islamist motive".Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has had another scarring effect.Germans pay some of the highest energy costs in Europe. The loss of access to cheap Russian energy that German car factories and other industries relied on, plus Donald Trump's trade tariffs and aggressive economic competition from China, have had a heavy toll on this country's export-driven economy.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, As the AfD squeezes the CDU on the right, the left wing Die Linke party attracts voters elsewhere Germany is Europe's, and therefore the eurozone currency's, largest economy. It is the world's largest single donor to Ukraine right now and it is the biggest net payer into the EU budget.When Germany's finances are in trouble and the country turns inward because of a political crisis, the knock-on effect beyond its borders can be considerable.Under financial pressure, Merz has been pushing hard, along with a group of other wealthier EU countries to slash their contributions to the bloc's budget, for example.This comes at a time when the EU wants to spend more, not less, on common defence projects, migration and AI and tech.Faced with perceived threats from Russia and China, wars in the Middle East affecting energy supplies and prices, plus the unpredictability - and many in Europe say, unreliability - of the US under Trump, now is a time Europeans must stick tightly together, says Brussels.The EU is watching Merz's travails, plus the strengthening of the AfD on the right and the hard left Die Linke too, with concern.These regional German votes come at the start of bumper election season across the EU, where all the big powers - (including France, Italy, Spain and Poland - go to the polls.Nationalist, Eurosceptic, anti-immigration parties are predicted to do well. And Beijing and Moscow are watching closely.

schema.headline: Friedrich Merz's political crisis threatens Germany's obsession with stability

title: 'Far from their best' to 'a joy to watch' -  ranking Premier League teams' start to season
description: There is now a three-week international break with no Premier League games until 10 October.We are five matches into the league season and there is a
body: There is now a three-week international break with no Premier League games until 10 October.We are five matches into the league season and there is a long way to go in the campaign, but which teams have impressed so far and who have disappointed?You can have your say in the comments at the bottom of the page.Arsenal: Solid start to their title defence until they were ripped apart by Brighton having survived a penalty scare at Sunderland. 7Aston Villa: Signs they are beginning to move in the right direction after losing so many key players during the transfer window. 6Bournemouth: If games lasted 80 minutes the Cherries would be near the top of the table. Need to cut out conceding so late. 6Brentford: Demolished Spurs and Chelsea without fuss during a highly impressive unbeaten start. Can they keep it up and challenge for Europe? 8Brighton: Kings of entertainment after hitting 16 goals in five top-flight games, including three against champions Arsenal. A joy to watch. 9 Chelsea: After a strong start under Xabi Alonso, the Blues have lost two of their past three - and were picked apart by Brentford. Are they really moving in the right direction? 6Coventry City: You could hear the sighs of relief in the away end at Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Will Frank Lampard's side kick on after that win? 6Crystal Palace: Room for improvement after one win and three defeats. 5Everton: Despite a transfer window to forget, David Moyes has made the Toffees hard to beat. 6 Fulham: Decent draws against Liverpool and Manchester United but need a win. Ipswich (away) followed by Hull (home), Coventry (away) and Crystal Palace (home) offer hope when they return from the international break. 5 Hull City: To have eight points from a tough opening five fixtures is an excellent return, including beating Manchester United and drawing with Aston Villa and Chelsea. 8Ipswich Town: Defensively vulnerable but two late winners, against Sunderland and Crystal Palace, have earned them six points and shown their fighting spirit. 5Leeds United: Fifth in the league, unbeaten and with the joint-best defensive record. They showed what they are capable of with a superb 4-1 win over Newcastle. 7Liverpool: Unbeaten but have been far from their best. Three clean sheets in their past three games, but more is expected from Andoni Iraola's side. 6Manchester City: Five league games, five victories. Managed to win at Manchester United despite going down to 10 men midway through the first half. With Erling Haaland already top scorer, City fans will expect a real push to win the league. 9Manchester United: Disappointing performances to lose at Hull and draw at a Fulham side who were bottom of the league. Their only win so far came against Ipswich and they were denied a victory at Everton by a late equaliser. 4Newcastle United: A mixed bag under new manager Matthias Jaissle. They impressed in a draw against Liverpool, won comfortably at Tottenham, but were also terrible in a loss at Leeds, although they responded well to beat Hull. 6Nottingham Forest: Their best results have come away, drawing at Liverpool and winning at Aston Villa. But their home form will be a huge worry - yet to score a goal and with only one point from three matches at the City Ground. 5Sunderland: After coming seventh in 2025-26, Sunderland fans will have wanted a better start to this season. The Black Cats gave good accounts of themselves against Arsenal and Manchester City, but lost both matches. 5Tottenham Hotspur: After spending more than £300m in the summer, Spurs have been poor, failing to score in their opening four league matches. Supporters will be demanding an instant improvement after the international break. 2

schema.headline: 'Far from their best' to 'a joy to watch' -  ranking Premier League teams' start to season

title: UK should 'team up' with Canada in new Europe alliance, Canadian minister says
description: Image source, Valerie Macon/AFP via Getty ImagesByEconomics editorThe UK should "team up" with a proposed economic alliance between Canada and Europe,
body: Image source, Valerie Macon/AFP via Getty ImagesByEconomics editorThe UK should "team up" with a proposed economic alliance between Canada and Europe, Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne has said."This is all about the substance, to build an alliance of the future," he told the BBC. "The world has changed. America has changed. So we need to change."Champagne also gave a frank assessment of the Canada-US trade war after a deal collapsed last month, saying the country had "stood up for our industries, our workers, our country" by imposing tariffs.His comments come after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed "opening the door" to an associate EU membership for Canada, an unprecedented move for the bloc.Figure caption, Watch: Is Canada about to join the EU?Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's visit to address the EU in Strasbourg, shortly after von der Leyen's proposal was made, was "to build the alliance of the future", Champagne said.Carney, the former governor of the Bank of England, has previously talked about an alliance of "middle powers" working together on economic growth, resilience and security.Champagne told the BBC that the UK and Canada had shared values."We need to look at partnership in a different way and the great thing is that when you look at Canada - and I would say the United Kingdom - we share the same values. We are very aligned in our vision of the world. Why don't we team up?" he said."We are independent and sovereign, but we are stronger together."After his return to the White House last year, US President Donald Trump imposed sweeping global tariffs, including on long-standing trade allies such as the UK.While the UK renegotiated a trade deal with the US in June last year, the new Canada-EU alliance does raise questions for the UK's post-Brexit positioning with Europe, as well as its position with the US, after some changes of presidential rhetoric over the Falklands and Irish unity in recent weeks.Carney met Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Liverpool in the middle of his trip to Brussels and Strasbourg last week, while Champagne attended a meeting of EU finance ministers in Dublin on Friday, alongside Chancellor John Healey.Figure caption, Watch: 'A better opportunity' - Canadians on a closer alliance with EuropeThe developing discussions around closer ties between the EU and Canada come as Ottawa remains locked in an escalating trade war with the US, with both sides imposing tit-for-tat tariffs after talks broke down at the last moment in August.Trump has also threatened further tariffs on the EU if the associate membership plan proved "hostile" to the US, calling the idea laughable and labelling Canada a "terrible trading partner".Champagne said the trade war was not a conflict chosen by Canada."We responded because at some stage you have to say 'enough is enough'. No one can infringe on our economic sovereignty... the world took notice," he said.The minister said Canada did not seek escalation after its "measured, targeted and strategic... dollar-for-dollar, tariff-for-tariff" response and the country would "re-engage at the right time" with its southern neighbour. Affected industries would be supported "as long as it takes and whatever it takes", he added.Champagne argued that Canada's strong fiscal position helped underpin its resilience, and that the dispute with the US provided a "golden opportunity" to diversify. This is the backdrop to the promise of an "alliance of the future" between Canada and the EU, and the idea of "teaming up" with the UK too.Burnham will meet Trump for the first time this week, in New York at the UN General Assembly.Last year, after his election, Carney invited King Charles to open the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa, a move widely seen as a rebuff to Trump's repeated suggestion that Commonwealth Canada could become part of the US.The detail of the offer made by the EU to negotiate "associate membership" for Canada is yet to be formalised.Champagne said this was "a moment of great opportunities" and to strengthen the existing relationship between Canada and the EU.Carney last week pointed to Canadian membership of EU university, scientific research, AI and defence funding schemes, as well as for young Canadians and Europeans to "cross the ocean and be able to study and live".He said Canada could supply critical minerals and gas and would seek access to European advanced technologies.It is understood that both Canada and the EU see the opportunity for a process for like-minded nations which might not ever be full members, for example Australia.Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

schema.headline: UK should 'team up' with Canada in new Europe alliance, Canadian minister says

title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban
description: Trump later reacted to news of the lawsuit, calling the news organisations "Third Rate Clowns" and "Crooked and Corrupt Press" that "trivialise and de
body: Trump later reacted to news of the lawsuit, calling the news organisations "Third Rate Clowns" and "Crooked and Corrupt Press" that "trivialise and demean" his achievements. "Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown 'sources,' shouldn't be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.He added that "almost without question" his team will file an appeal.The First Amendment forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press - language that courts have traditionally interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage.The statement from CNN, Politico and MS NOW said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting."Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."The media organisations filed the lawsuit on Monday in US District Court in Washington, asking a judge to quickly rule Trump's ban unconstitutional and prevent his aides from enforcing it.On Monday morning, major US TV networks pulled out of White House pool duties, which sees media organisations share material with each other to save on costs and space when broadcasting presidential events to the American public.Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who currently holds a rotating role helping to organise media TV crews covering the White House, wrote in an email seen by the BBC that "effective today, the TV pool will not be covering designated as pool coverage" of President Trump.The message said the move followed the White House "preventing" CNN from fulfilling its pool duties for Trump's trip to New York and that "there will be no replacement pool put in place".CNN - one of only five US news outlets in the White House press pool for live television - was originally due to cover Trump's trip to the UN General Assembly in New York on Monday and Tuesday.But on Monday morning, the five-seat CNN booth in the basement of the White House press area - typically manned throughout the day from the early hours of the morning - was empty and closed. Screens and monitors inside were turned off.Instead, a CNN crew was outside the secured area of the White House grounds, broadcasting live from a public pavement.Five TV networks, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC, issued a joint statement: "The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government."No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting."Those five networks are considered the only ones with the money and infrastructure to distribute live coverage from the White House and presidential events.For now, the White House media slot has remained vacant and instead the conservative TV outlet, Real America's Voice, was listed as "secondary" crew on Trump's trip to New York, where he will meet Mayor Zohran Mamdani and French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday.Announcing his ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW last week, Trump did not mention specific stories or reporting that prompted the move, but later said "it's really just cumulative stories over the last few years".The US president added that there "may be others to join them".When later asked by a reporter what he meant by this, Trump responded: "Others to come in terms of fake news? Well, you know, the New York Times is fake news, the Washington Post is fake news."In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool which has access to Trump and had for more than a century been managed by the White House Correspondents' Association.The same month, the administration moved to bar Associated Press (AP) reporters and photographers from spaces where access is limited, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because of the outlet's usage of the term "Gulf of Mexico" instead of "Gulf of America". AP filed a lawsuit and the case remains ongoing.There have been a few instances of other administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.But after pushback from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was granted access. But unlike with Trump's exclusion of CNN, MS Now and Politico, the Obama administration did not try to bar Fox News from all pool coverage, just one specific interview.Trump has been frequently critical of news organisations and his administration has launched legal action against a series of outlets, including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal and the BBC.Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multi-million-dollar settlements. Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing.

schema.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban

title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
description: Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen say they carried out drone and ballistic missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as energy sites on
body: Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen say they carried out drone and ballistic missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as energy sites on the country's Red Sea coast.Saudi authorities said they intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh on Saturday, without confirming any further strikes or causalities. Earlier, a column of black smoke was seen rising from fuel tanks near the Saudi capital's international airport, where flights were disrupted temporarily on Saturday. Air raid alerts had sounded in the capital for the first time since the Iran-backed Houthis increased their attacks on Saudi Arabia in July.The US state department urged Americans in the Middle East to "exercise vigilance and be prepared for potential flight cancellations and other travel disruptions"."Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," it said in a statement. It added that Americans "should seriously reconsider travel to and through the region".Air defences also stopped "hostile attempts to target civilians" in the cities of Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, an official spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said in a statement.In a statement posted online, Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said a "large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" had been used to attack "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and Aramco state oil and gas company facilities in Yanbu on the coast.  He added that the attacks were "in response to the Saudi enemy's criminal attempts" to target the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which is currently controlled by the Houthis.Earlier, Sarea had accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week.The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen.According to an unconfirmed report from AFP news agency, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday.The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency.      On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external.A number of apparent explosions were heard in Riyadh and major problems were reported at King Khalid International Airport earlier on Saturday, with the tracking website FlightRadar24 reporting delays and cancellations., externalAn AFP journalist reported that firefighters could be seen trying to extinguish the flames of a burnt-out fuel tank belonging to Aramco.The Saudi Civil Defence had sent out phone alerts overnight warning of potential danger in Riyadh and other regions, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning.Residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they had heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through the city after the alerts."I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," said a resident of northern Riyadh, 27. "It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this."The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe.The group said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.      On Friday, investment banking giant JP Morgan said it was struggling to predict how oil prices would be impacted by the war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame".

schema.headline: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
